# Fix `worklog_dir_flag` worktree resolution for worktrees under `<main>/.worklog/worktrees`

> **Provenance:** transferred from `CG-0MVZKL4WB000JPZT` (Tableau-Card-Engine
> store) by producer decision, where it was `discovered-from:CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY`
> (TCE worktree `wl-CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY-retire-legacy-choice-fields-and-the-clar`,
> commit `4975f6ff`), observed while running
> `render_report.py CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY` from that worktree. The CG item is
> deleted after transfer; the full intake brief lives here.

## Problem statement

`shared/status_lifecycle._detect_worklog_dir()` builds ancestor candidates as
`parent / ".worklog"` for **every** parent, so when the cwd sits inside
`<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` the ancestor `<main>/.worklog`
itself yields `<main>/.worklog/.worklog`; it also accepts any `.worklog`
directory **without** checking that it is initialised. Both defects make
`worklog_dir_flag()` hand `wl` a store root that is either non-existent
(no-op flag) or uninitialised (`wl` fails with
`"Worklog system is not initialized"`), so skill scripts that shell out to
`wl` break when run from an `implement.py` worktree.

## Users

- **AI agent running skill scripts from an implement worktree** — `/skill:report`,
  `/skill:audit`, `persist_audit.py`, and status/lifecycle helpers all resolve
  the store through `worklog_dir_flag()` / `resolve_worklog_flags()`.
  Story: *As an agent finishing work in a worktree, `render_report.py <id>`
  must read the main checkout's worklog so my report is populated and my
  status transition is written to the store the producer reads.*
- **Producer / operator** — needs a trustworthy store resolution so a run from
  a worktree cannot silently target a wrong or uninitialised store.
  Story: *As the producer, when an agent reports from a worktree, the item it
  reports on must be the item in the main checkout's store, with no manual
  `--worklog-dir` correction.*
- **Skill maintainer** — needs the resolution rule pinned by tests.
  Story: *As a skill maintainer, I need a regression test for the
  `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/…` layout so a future refactor of the ancestor
  walk cannot reintroduce a nested `.worklog/.worklog` path.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — worktree root resolves to the main checkout store.**
      With cwd = `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` and no `.worklog`
      in the worktree, `worklog_dir_flag()` returns
      `["--worklog-dir", "<main>/.worklog"]` (the initialised store), including
      when a stale `<main>/.worklog/.worklog` directory exists.
- [ ] **AC2 — no double suffix.** An ancestor directory already named
      `.worklog` is never extended to `.worklog/.worklog`; the worklog
      directory that is itself an ancestor is the candidate.
- [ ] **AC3 — initialised candidates only.** A candidate `.worklog` that is not
      initialised (`_is_initialized_worklog()` false — e.g. a worktree's
      committed `config.yaml`-only copy) is never returned; resolution
      continues to the nearest initialised ancestor, and returns `[]` (no flag)
      rather than an uninitialised path when nothing initialised exists.
- [ ] **AC4 — unit tests cover the worktree layouts.** New hermetic tests
      (tmp_path fixtures, no real `git worktree`, no network) covering:
      (a) `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` with a stale
      `<main>/.worklog/.worklog` present;
      (b) a **subdirectory** of a worktree whose committed `.worklog/` holds
      only `config.yaml` (the uninitialised-candidate case);
      (c) a plain nested project cwd (no `.worklog` between cwd and the project
      root) still resolving as today (no regression).
- [ ] **AC5 — existing precedence preserved, no weakening.** Precedence
      `explicit --worklog-dir` > prefix-to-sibling scan > cwd chain > no flag is
      unchanged, and the existing tests in
      `skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py` pass without
      edits to their assertions.
- [ ] **AC6 — documentation.** The resolution rule (initialised-only, no
      `.worklog/.worklog` nesting, worktree-ancestor special case) is stated in
      the code docstrings of `_detect_worklog_dir()` / `worklog_dir_flag()` and
      in `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` (the section that says
      `StatusLifecycle` resolves the worklog dir automatically) and
      `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md` (the worklog-store resolution note).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Fix lands in this repository.** The defective code is
  `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` here; `~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to
  `skill/`. Do **not** edit another project's `.pi/`, and do not create a
  vendored copy of the helper.
- **Shared seam.** `status_lifecycle` is imported by every skill; keep the
  change narrow (one candidate-selection helper reused by both
  `_detect_worklog_dir()` and `worklog_dir_flag()`), with no behaviour change
  for cwds that already resolve correctly.
- **Fail closed, never guess.** Returning no `--worklog-dir` (so `wl` reports
  the real error) is preferred over returning a path that is not an initialised
  store.
- **Hermetic tests.** No real `git worktree`/network in the unit tests;
  `unittest.mock.patch` on `Path.cwd`-derived inputs or `tmp_path` layouts,
  matching the existing test module's style.
- **Gate order.** build → test → commit, never reversed; no ad-hoc `pytest` —
  run tests through the test skill (`/skill:test` / `run_tests.py`).

## Existing state (verified during intake)

- Source of truth: `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` (this repo).
- `_detect_worklog_dir()` (line ~258) order: `<cwd>/.worklog` →
  `<git toplevel>/.worklog` → `for parent in cwd.parents: parent/".worklog"`;
  the last two gates call `is_dir()` only, never `_is_initialized_worklog()`.
- `worklog_dir_flag()` (line ~391) has a **second, different** ancestor walk
  that *does* check `_is_initialized_worklog()`, then falls back to
  `_detect_worklog_dir()` — so the two walks disagree.
- Reproduced (Tableau-Card-Engine checkout, registered worktree, git toplevel =
  the worktree):
  ```
  cwd=/home/rgardler/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine/.worklog/worktrees/wl-CG-0MRBDPFPH009Y8M0-balance-tooling
  _detect_worklog_dir() -> /home/rgardler/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine/.worklog/.worklog
  worklog_dir_flag()    -> ['--worklog-dir', '…/Tableau-Card-Engine/.worklog/.worklog']
  ```
  The stale `…/.worklog/.worklog/` exists and contains only a `worktrees/`
  subdirectory (no `initialized` marker, no `worklog.db`).
- Reproduced (this repository, registered worktree, run from a **subdirectory**
  so the `cwd/.worklog` branch is skipped):
  ```
  cwd=…/.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MSQ8MXXI0029B5M-…/skill
  _detect_worklog_dir() -> <that worktree>/.worklog      # config.yaml only — NOT initialised
  worklog_dir_flag()    -> ['--worklog-dir', '<worktree>/.worklog']
  ```
  i.e. a second manifestation of the same defect (uninitialised candidate),
  at the worktree **root** even though the initialised main store is a direct
  ancestor. Both are in scope via AC1–AC3.
- `_resolve_repo_root()` already handles the worktree case for the framework
  root (`skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py::TestFrameworkRootDerivation`)
  — the framework root is correct; only the *store* resolution is wrong.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py` covers prefix scan,
  `resolve_worklog_dir`, `resolve_worklog_flags` precedence and `run_wl`
  injection, but has **no** ancestor-walk / worktree-layout test.
- `skill/shared/worklog_sync.py` re-uses `worklog_dir_flag()`, so it is fixed
  transitively. `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` resolves its own target
  project root and is unaffected.
- Adjacent same-class defect, **filed separately** by producer decision as
  `SA-0MW0JI376007RON7` (see *Related work*):
  `skill/shared/code_freeze.py::_detect_worklog_dir()` (line
  ~48) duplicates the ancestor walk with the same `parent/".worklog"`
  construction and no initialisation check, so `code_freeze_marker_path()`
  would read `<main>/.worklog/.worklog/code-freeze.json` from a worktree.

## Desired change

1. Introduce one candidate-selection helper used by both
   `_detect_worklog_dir()` and `worklog_dir_flag()`:
   - for each ancestor, if the ancestor **is** a worklog directory
     (`name == ".worklog"`), the candidate is that ancestor itself; otherwise
     the candidate is `ancestor / ".worklog"`;
   - only accept a candidate when `_is_initialized_worklog(candidate)` is true
     (in the `_detect_worklog_dir` gate; `worklog_dir_flag` keeps its existing
     "no flag" contract when nothing initialised is found).
2. Delete the duplicated walk in `worklog_dir_flag()` in favour of the shared
   helper (no second, divergent rule).
3. Tests per AC4, in the existing
   `skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py` module style.
4. Doc updates per AC6.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — `_detect_worklog_dir()` (~line 258)
  gains the `.worklog`-named-ancestor rule and the `_is_initialized_worklog()`
  gate; `worklog_dir_flag()` (~line 391) re-uses the same helper instead of its
  own walk; docstrings per AC6.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py` — new
  `TestWorklogDirAncestorWalk` class with the AC4 cases.
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — the "`StatusLifecycle` resolves the same
  directory automatically" paragraph (~lines 84–88) gains the initialised-only /
  no-nesting rule.
- `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md` — worklog-store resolution note
  (~lines 360–364).

## Related work

- `SA-0MVK2G09X00239YL` (open, intake_complete) — *implement.py finish reports
  status changes that the main worklog store does not show*. Same seam, wider
  scope (finish must pass an explicit store). Its "Existing state" note claims
  `worklog_dir_flag` "does resolve the main checkout store from a worktree";
  the evidence above shows that holds only when no stale
  `<main>/.worklog/.worklog` exists — this item carries the counter-example.
  Partial overlap only, so **not** a duplicate.
- `SA-0MW0JI376007RON7` — `code_freeze.py` resolves a worktree's
  non-initialised `.worklog` (the same walk duplicated in `code_freeze.py`).
  Filed separately by producer decision (Appendix Q2) and **blocked by** this
  item, so the shared rule lands first.
- `CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY` (Tableau-Card-Engine) — original discovery work item.
- `CG-0MUC5GVCJ0062BN7` (Tableau-Card-Engine, completed) — earlier
  worktree-resolution defect (`.pi/test-config.json` unseen from a worktree):
  same failure family, different file.
- `SA-0MSG57UNY009DE51`, `SA-0MSGH55OJ003WKYZ`, `SA-0MTOMCML900254CI`
  (completed) — the prefix-to-sibling seam and cwd-independence lineage this
  item extends.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: resolver regression elsewhere.** Other skills rely on
  `_detect_worklog_dir()` returning a non-initialised directory in exotic
  layouts. Mitigation: AC5 requires the existing suite to pass unchanged; the
  change only *narrows* accepted candidates, and `worklog_dir_flag()` keeps its
  "no flag" fallback so `wl` still reports its own error.
- **Risk: `.worklog`-named ancestor inside a normal project** (e.g. a directory
  literally called `.worklog` used for something else). Mitigation: the
  `.worklog`-named ancestor is only accepted when `_is_initialized_worklog()`
  is true.
- **Risk: styling split between the two walks** if only one is fixed.
  Mitigation: single shared helper (Desired change 1–2).
- **Scope-creep risk: fixing `code_freeze.py` in the same change.** Excluded by
  producer decision (Appendix Q2) — it is filed separately.
- **Assumption:** the "stale `<main>/.worklog/.worklog`" directory is a local
  artefact (from an old run) and is not committed anywhere; the fix must not
  depend on its removal, because the nesting rule is wrong regardless.
- **Assumption:** unit tests can express the layout with `tmp_path` +
  `mock.patch` rather than creating real git worktrees (the existing module
  already models the framework-root worktree layout this way).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Where should the fix and its record land?** The defective code lives
  in SorraAgents (`skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`); the TCE checkout has no
  `skill/` tree, so a TCE `implement.py` worktree could not carry the change
  (the TCE-side `implement.py finish` fails closed on out-of-worktree edits).
  Options were: (a) transfer the item to the SA store; (b) create an SA item
  carrying code + tests, keep the CG item as a linked discovery record;
  (c) commit to SorraAgents `dev` from outside a worktree (breaks
  worktree-isolation). Agent recommendation: (b).
  **Answer (producer):** *"SA create there then delete this item"* — create the
  SA item with the full brief (this item) **and delete** the CG item, i.e. a
  transfer rather than a linked pair. Source: operator reply in the intake
  session `herdr-1793666897-1472625-2858`.
- **Q2 — Fold in the adjacent `code_freeze.py` defect?** Options: (a) fix both
  in this change via one shared helper; (b) keep this item narrow and file the
  `code_freeze` fix as a separate `discovered-from` item. Agent recommendation:
  (b).

# `code_freeze.py` resolves a worktree's non-initialised `.worklog` (and can build `.worklog/.worklog`)

> **Provenance:** `discovered-from:SA-0MW0JHMJE006GWQB` (which was transferred
> from `CG-0MVZKL4WB000JPZT`, itself `discovered-from:CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY`).
> Filed separately by producer decision so the parent fix stays narrow.

## Problem statement

`skill/shared/code_freeze.py` carries its **own** copy of
`_detect_worklog_dir()`. It builds ancestor candidates as `parent / ".worklog"`
for every parent and accepts any `.worklog` directory without checking that it
is initialised. Consequences:

- from a linked worktree root whose committed `.worklog/` holds only
  `config.yaml`, `code_freeze_marker_path()` returns
  `<worktree>/.worklog/code-freeze.json` — a marker file that can never exist,
  so the fail-closed freeze gate silently sees "no freeze";
- from `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` (no committed `.worklog`), a
  stale `<main>/.worklog/.worklog` directory would be selected, giving
  `<main>/.worklog/.worklog/code-freeze.json`.

The correct marker in both cases is `<main>/.worklog/code-freeze.json`.

## Users

- **AI agent running `/skill:implement` from a worktree** — the implement
  workflow consults the code-freeze marker; reading the wrong path makes the
  freeze gate miss an active freeze.
  Story: *As an implementing agent in a worktree, an active code freeze must be
  detected, so I stop instead of landing a commit that the freeze forbids.*
- **Producer/operator** — an activated freeze must be effective immediately for
  every checkout.
  Story: *As the producer, when I activate a freeze, agents working in
  worktrees must observe it without extra `--worklog-dir` instructions.*
- **Skill maintainer** — needs one resolution rule, not two divergent copies.
  Story: *As a maintainer, code-freeze marker resolution must not silently drift
  from `status_lifecycle`'s worklog-dir rule.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — worktree root resolves the main marker.** With cwd at a linked
      worktree root that has a committed, **uninitialised** `.worklog/`
      (`config.yaml` only), `code_freeze_marker_path()` returns
      `<main>/.worklog/code-freeze.json`.
- [ ] **AC2 — no `.worklog/.worklog` nesting.** With cwd inside
      `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>`, the marker path is
      `<main>/.worklog/code-freeze.json` even when a stale
      `<main>/.worklog/.worklog/` directory exists.
- [ ] **AC3 — explicit `project_root` unchanged.** `code_freeze_marker_path(<root>)`
      still returns `<root>/.worklog/code-freeze.json` and is unaffected by the
      cwd-based rule.
- [ ] **AC4 — one rule, not two.** `code_freeze._detect_worklog_dir()` either
      re-uses the shared resolution helper from `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`
      (preferred — no duplicated walk) or mirrors it exactly, with a comment
      naming the shared rule as authoritative.
- [ ] **AC5 — unit tests.** Hermetic `tmp_path` tests in
      `skill/shared/tests/test_code_freeze.py` for AC1–AC3 (no real
      `git worktree`, no network), alongside the existing marker tests.
- [ ] **AC6 — documentation.** The `code_freeze.py` docstrings state the
      initialised-only / no-nesting rule; if resolution is shared, note it in
      `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` next to the `StatusLifecycle` note.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Do not widen the freeze semantics: this is a path-resolution fix, not a
  change to how a freeze is activated, cleared, or enforced.
- Keep the existing public API (`code_freeze_marker_path`, marker read/write
  helpers) and their `project_root` behaviour unchanged.
- Prefer re-using the shared helper over a second walk; if that would create a
  circular import, mirror the rule and reference the canonical one in a
  comment.
- Gate order: build → test → commit; no ad-hoc `pytest` — run tests through the
  test skill (`/skill:test` / `run_tests.py`).

## Existing state (verified during intake of the parent item)

- `skill/shared/code_freeze.py::_detect_worklog_dir()` (~line 48) order:
  explicit `project_root` → `<cwd>/.worklog` → `<git toplevel>/.worklog` →
  `for parent in cwd.parents: parent/".worklog"`, each gated on `is_dir()` only.
- `code_freeze_marker_path()` (~line 90) uses that helper and falls back to
  `<cwd>/.worklog/code-freeze.json` when nothing resolves.
- The same candidate-construction defect is proven in
  `status_lifecycle._detect_worklog_dir()` (parent item
  `SA-0MW0JHMJE006GWQB`, AC1–AC3) — this item is the same rule applied to the
  code-freeze copy.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/shared/code_freeze.py` — `_detect_worklog_dir()` / marker path
  resolution (~lines 48–101).
- `skill/shared/tests/test_code_freeze.py` — new worktree-layout cases
  (AC1–AC3).
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — one sentence alongside the
  `StatusLifecycle` resolution note (if the rule is shared).
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — only if the shared helper is exported
  for reuse (no behaviour change expected here).

## Related work

- `SA-0MW0JHMJE006GWQB` — parent fix for `status_lifecycle._detect_worklog_dir()`
  / `worklog_dir_flag()` (same rule, `wl`-facing seam). This item should land
  after it so the shared rule exists.
- `CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY`, `CG-0MVZKL4WB000JPZT` (Tableau-Card-Engine) —
  discovery chain for the original defect.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: freeze bypass stays latent** until this item is implemented, if the
  parent fix lands alone. Mitigation: the parent item's docs state the
  code-freeze copy is still defective and link here.
- **Risk: duplicated rule drifts again.** Mitigation: AC4 prefers the shared
  helper.
- **Scope-creep risk:** touching freeze activation/enforcement or adding new
  marker features — out of scope; record such ideas as separate items.
- **Assumption:** the implement workflow's freeze check is the only consumer of
  `code_freeze_marker_path()`; verified by grep during implementation.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Fold this into the parent `worklog_dir_flag` fix?**
  **Answer (producer):** *"file separately"* — filed here; the parent item stays
  narrow. Source: operator reply in the intake session
  `herdr-1793666897-1472625-2858`, relayed via
  `SA-0MW0JHMJE006GWQB` (Appendix Q2).

## Problem statement

The audit pipeline currently treats *any* failing test as a failure of the audit: a red F3 auto-execution leaves execution-dependent ACs `partial` (so `Ready to close: No`), and a red merge-gate suite run fails the integration closed. That is the right behaviour for the release gate, but it is wrong for the everyday audits an agent runs while implementing a work item: unrelated, pre-existing red unit tests (e.g. another item's broken test) block an otherwise complete item and send the audit into a remediation loop that cannot succeed.

Audits must therefore support two test-failure modes: **strict** (today's behaviour — any failing test fails the audit) and **permissive** (a failing **unit** test that is provably *not affected in any way* by the audited work item's changes does not fail the audit; integration/end-to-end failures always fail).

## Users

- **Agent implementing a work item** — "As an agent running `/skill:audit` on my in-progress item, I want an unrelated red unit test elsewhere in the repo not to block my item, so that I do not chase failures outside my change set."
- **Release engineer (ship skill)** — "As the release gate, I want every audited item to have a genuinely green suite, so that `dev` is never promoted to `main` on the back of excused failures."
- **Producer reviewing an audit** — "As a reviewer, I want the persisted audit report to state which mode was used and, for every excused failure, the evidence that it was unrelated, so that I can trust a permissive pass."

Example user stories:

- Permissive: `tests/test_other_skill.py::test_unrelated` fails; the item only touched `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`; the audit still returns `Ready to close: Yes` with the failure listed as excused (unrelated, unit) and a critical `test-failure` work item created.
- Strict: the same failure blocks the audit; ship re-runs the item under `--strict` and refuses to release.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Mode resolution and default.** `audit_runner.py issue` (and `batch`) accepts `--strict` / `--no-strict`, with `AUDIT_STRICT=1` as the environment equivalent; **the default is permissive**. Precedence is flag > env > default, resolved once and recorded. Unit tests cover the precedence matrix and that `--strict` reproduces today's verdict for a red suite (any failure ⇒ `Ready to close: No`).
2. **Permissive excusal — unrelated unit failures.** In permissive mode, a red suite whose failures are **all** unit-classified **and** proven unrelated to the item's changes does not fail the audit: the runner injects a "run red, excused failures" evidence block into the Phase 1/Phase 2 prompts (so execution-dependent ACs may be marked `met`), the report gains a `## Test Failure Mode` section listing every excused failure with its classification and relatedness evidence, and the `--json` payload carries the same data. Unit tests cover the excused path end-to-end at the verdict level.
3. **Permissive fail-closed cases.** In permissive mode the audit still fails when (a) any failure is integration/end-to-end classified, (b) any unit failure is affected by the item's changes, or (c) relatedness is inconclusive and no baseline comparison can be performed. Unit tests cover each case individually, plus the mixed case (one excusable + one blocking failure ⇒ audit fails).
4. **Scope classification and relatedness algorithm.** Failures are classified by path convention (`tests/integration/**`, `tests/e2e/**`, `tests/manual/**`, `**/*_e2e*`, `**/*integration*` ⇒ integration/end-to-end; everything else ⇒ unit; unclassifiable ⇒ integration, fail closed). Relatedness is decided by deterministic mapping first (failing test file ∈ item's changed files; a module the test imports ∈ changed files; a changed shared test-infrastructure file such as `conftest.py`/`tests/helpers/**`), then — only for inconclusive failures — by a baseline re-run of just those failures in a scratch worktree at the item's pre-change commit (fails identically ⇒ unrelated; passes ⇒ affected). Unit tests cover the pattern table, the import-mapping step, and the baseline comparison (both outcomes), with no real suite execution.
5. **Triage is preserved.** Excused failures are still triaged into critical `test-failure` work items (same dedup + cap semantics as today). Unit tests assert triage is invoked for excused failures as well as blocking ones.
6. **Ship uses strict mode.** All three ship audit call sites (`check-audit-gate.js`, `check-final-validation.js`, `refresh-audits.js`) pass `--strict`, and the manual remediation commands they surface include `--strict`. Tests assert the constructed command strings; the flag name is generic (`--strict`, not `--strict-tests`) so future strictness checks can share it.
7. **Freshness respects mode strength.** A strict run must never reuse a stored permissive "Yes" (it re-runs); a permissive run may reuse a stored strict "Yes". Unit tests cover both directions.
8. **Documentation and validation.** `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `skill/ship/SKILL.md` and `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` document both modes, the flag/env precedence, the classification and relatedness rules, and which callers use which mode. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Read-only mandate:** the audit stays read-only except for the existing sanctioned exceptions. The baseline comparison runs only the failing tests, in a scratch worktree (never the main checkout), through the existing paced runner (`run_tests.paced_runner()`) and under the existing `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` stand-down so nested suite runs cannot recurse.
- **Strict mode must be byte-for-byte today's behaviour** — no verdict change for existing strict callers.
- **Never-block guarantee (F4) is preserved:** the mode never introduces a hard exit for infrastructure failure; inability to classify or baseline degrades to *affected* (fail closed on the verdict), never a crash.
- **The dev-push pre-push full-suite gate is unchanged** — permissive mode does not weaken it; it only governs the audit verdict.
- **Determinism:** the excusal decision must be reproducible from the persisted report alone (mode, classification, mapping/baseline evidence recorded).
- **No new suite executions on the happy path:** a green suite behaves exactly as today; excusal work happens only when the suite is red.
- Scope-creep guard: any richer relatedness heuristic (e.g. coverage-based mapping), or per-repo `unitTestGlobs`/`integrationTestGlobs` configuration, is out of scope — record it as a linked follow-up if it turns out to be needed.

## Existing state

- `_run_tests_via_test_skill()` (F3 auto-execution) parses failures, triages them, and returns `success`; a red run injects **no** GREEN-RUN block, so execution-dependent ACs stay `partial` ⇒ `Ready to close: No`. Red cached entries (`_classify_full_suite_cache` → `red`) also stay partial with no execution.
- `_integrate_into_dev()` (Phase 1 merge gate) runs `run_suite("all")`; `success == False` ⇒ `Integration failed: test suite failed.` ⇒ audit fails closed.
- Green evidence reaches the parent Phase-1 screen, both child Phase-1 screens and every Phase 2 prompt (`_green_run_prompt_block`, `_auto_green_run_prompt_block`, `_test_skill_run_prompt_block`).
- The freshness gate fingerprints `{title_hash, description_hash}` only — it has no notion of *how* a verdict was produced, so a permissive "Yes" would currently satisfy ship's strict re-run.
- Item changed-file resolution already exists (`_resolve_touched_files`, `_extract_key_files`); failure parsing exists (`parse_pytest_failures`, `parse_node_failures`); suite resolution exists (`full_suite_commands`).
- Ship invokes the runner from `check-audit-gate.js:841`, `check-final-validation.js:479`, `refresh-audits.js:131` (`runAuditCommand` defaults), plus the surfaced manual commands in `check-audit-gate.js:386/518/638` and `audit-remediation.js:43`.
- `pytest.ini` declares only `smoke`/`critical`/`benchmark` markers; the repo has no `integration`/`e2e` markers, and `tests/integration/*.mjs` exists — path convention is the practical classifier.

## Desired change

**Headline:** add a `--strict` audit mode (permissive by default) in which only *unrelated unit* failures are excused, and make the ship release gate audit strictly.

1. **Mode plumbing.** New `--strict` / `--no-strict` flags on `issue` and `batch`, `AUDIT_STRICT` env var, default permissive; a resolved `strict: bool` on `_AuditContext`, threaded to the F3 path, the merge gate, the prompt evidence builders, the report assembler and the `--json` payload.
2. **Failure classification + relatedness module** (helpers in `audit_runner.py`):
   - `_classify_test_failure_scope(failure)` → `"unit"` | `"integration"` from the path-pattern table (fail closed to `integration`).
   - `_failure_relatedness(failure, touched_files, key_files, project_root)` → `"affected"` | `"unrelated"` | `"inconclusive"` (test file match, import scan against changed modules, shared test-infrastructure match).
   - `_baseline_unrelated(failures, project_root, baseline_commit)` → per-failure verdicts by re-running only the inconclusive failures in a scratch worktree at the pre-change commit.
3. **Verdict integration.** A single helper (e.g. `_evaluate_red_suite(...)`) that, in strict mode, returns "blocked" for any failure, and in permissive mode returns `blocked` (with reasons) or `excused` (with per-failure evidence). Both the F3 path and the merge gate consume it. Excused-red injects an evidence block analogous to the GREEN-RUN blocks; blocked-red keeps today's behaviour and diagnostics.
4. **Cached-red handling (consistency).** In permissive mode a `red` cached full-suite entry is classified from the cached output (already stored) rather than being accepted as blocking-by-default; if the cached output yields no parseable failure records the runner executes the suite as it does on a miss. Strict mode keeps today's cached-red behaviour unchanged.
5. **Persistence and report.** `## Test Failure Mode` section (mode, resolution source, per-failure classification/relatedness/evidence, baseline commit used); `--json` payload key `test_failure_mode`; the mode is part of the stored audit so the freshness gate can compare mode strength (strict re-runs over permissive; permissive may reuse strict).
6. **Ship wiring.** `--strict` added to the three ship runner invocations and the surfaced manual remediation commands.
7. **Docs.** Audit + ship SKILL files and their `docs/dev/*-reference.md` companions updated with the contract, the default, and the caller matrix.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — mode resolution/plumbing; `_classify_test_failure_scope`, `_failure_relatedness`, `_baseline_unrelated`, `_evaluate_red_suite`; excused-red evidence block; `_run_tests_via_test_skill` and `_integrate_into_dev` integration; report + `--json` sections; freshness mode-strength comparison.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — document both modes, the `--strict`/`AUDIT_STRICT` precedence, default, classification/relatedness rules, caller matrix.
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — full contract: pattern table, relatedness algorithm, baseline worktree rules, cached-red behaviour, mode-strength freshness.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` — `runAuditCommand` default + surfaced manual commands gain `--strict`.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js` — `runAuditCommand` default gains `--strict`.
- `skill/ship/scripts/refresh-audits.js` — pre-flight refresh `runAuditCommand` gains `--strict`.
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — state that ship audits strictly.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_strict_mode.py` (new) — mode precedence, classification table, relatedness mapping, baseline comparison, excused/blocked verdicts, triage-on-excusal, cached-red behaviour, freshness mode strength.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py` — extend existing F3/merge-gate coverage for the strict path parity.
- `skill/ship/tests/test_audit_strict_flag.mjs` (new) — command-string assertions for the three ship call sites.
- `command/audit.md` — note that the default is permissive and `--strict` is available (optional, if the prompt enumerates flags).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: excusal hides a real regression.** Mitigated by fail-closed defaults (integration always fails; affected or inconclusive always fails) and by recording per-failure evidence in the persisted report.
- **Risk: baseline worktree cost/instability** (merge-base unresolvable, worktree add failure, test absent at baseline). Mitigated: baseline runs only the inconclusive failures, and any baseline failure ⇒ treated as affected (fail closed) with the reason recorded.
- **Risk: a permissive "Yes" leaks into the release.** Mitigated by AC6 (ship passes `--strict`) and AC7 (strict never reuses a permissive verdict).
- **Risk: recursion/concurrency** — the baseline run must reuse `paced_runner()` and honour `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE`; tests must mock subprocess execution (per the shared test-writing guidelines: no real suite, no real `audit_runner.py issue` child).
- **Assumption:** "integration/end-to-end" is identified by path convention in this repo (no markers exist); richer classification (markers, per-repo globs) is a follow-up if needed.
- **Assumption:** excused failures still create critical `test-failure` items (triage behaviour unchanged).
- **Assumption:** the merge gate proceeds with integration in permissive mode when the only failures are excused, recording them in the merge-gate evidence (strict keeps failing closed).
- **Assumption:** `--strict` is a generic audit-strictness flag; future strictness checks may join it, so the flag is not named after tests.

## Related work

### Related work items

- **SA-0MSAAUJ1F0026BMN** – Create 'test' skill: run tests, triage failures, validate & fix test usefulness (completed) — the suite execution/triage machinery this change consumes (`run_tests.py`, `parse_pytest_failures`, `check_or_create`).
- **SA-0MUIULX49001BWGG** – Release-gate fail-fast on repository-override vars (completed) — precedent for the release gate taking the conservative path while other callers stay convenient.
- **SA-0MPFD4T0F004RI8I** – CI: Add end-to-end packaging/installation verification for packages/tui (completed) — the end-to-end tests that must never be excused.
- **SA-0MSTN5KRF0097TVP** – F3 default auto-execution on cache miss (referenced throughout `skill/audit/SKILL.md`; the item is not present in this store) — the path whose red result becomes mode-dependent here.
- **SA-0MT456M27001LRTL** – Phase 1 merge gate (referenced throughout `skill/audit/SKILL.md`; the item is not present in this store) — the second red-suite path in scope.
- **SA-0MVIDI8E00063OOP** – Fingerprint from item data only, v2 line (completed) — the freshness gate extended here with mode strength.
- **SA-0MVR9B1UH002BUST** – Audit runner: preserve a producer's review across passing re-audits (open) — touches the same audit-runner verdict/lifecycle surface; check for conflicts when implementing.
- **SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81** – Audit accepts gate-produced full-suite evidence (completed) — the read-only green-evidence path that permissive mode must not weaken.

### Repository file matches

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — the pipeline being extended.
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — audit contract documentation.
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — suite execution, cache scope and triage semantics consumed by the audit.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (mode switch location):** strict default + `--permissive-tests` opt-in / **permissive default + `--strict` in ship** / env-var only. — **Answer (producer, interactive):** option **b** — permissive is the default and ship passes the strict flag; the flag is named **`--strict`** (not `--strict-tests`) so future strictness requirements can share it. Source: interactive reply, this session.
- **Q2 (relatedness test):** deterministic path+import mapping / merge-base baseline re-run / **hybrid**. — **Answer (producer, interactive):** option **c** — deterministic mapping decides the clear cases; only inconclusive failures get the baseline re-run. Source: interactive reply, this session.
- **Q3 (unit vs integration classification):** **path convention** / pytest markers / configurable globs in `.pi/test-config.json`. — **Answer (producer, interactive):** option **a** — path convention. Source: interactive reply, this session. Research: `pytest.ini` declares only `smoke`/`critical`/`benchmark` markers, so marker-based classification has no data to work with today; `tests/integration/*.mjs` exists and is matched by the convention.
- **Assumptions put to the producer (no objection recorded):** excused failures are still triaged into critical `test-failure` items and recorded in the report; the mode applies to both the F3 auto-execution and the merge-gate suite paths; the mode and its basis are surfaced in the persisted report and the `--json` payload.

## Goal

Investigate, and then reduce, large tool-call results before they enter conversation history, so that a single oversized tool result does not inflate every subsequent model turn. Prefer the cheapest effective mechanism; a small-model compaction call is one candidate among several.

## Evidence (from the proxy incident 2026-11-03, LLM repo)

- A single tool-role message of 51,945 bytes (a full SKILL.md pasted into history by the audit skill) entered the conversation at 08:41:54. The conversation grew from 22 KB to 120 KB of content over 7 turns, and the prompt went 6,564 to 33,570 tokens.
- Every subsequent turn re-prefilled the growing tail on a local model measuring 143-303 tok/s prefill, producing 53 s and 72 s time-to-first-byte.
- The proxy priced that 51,945-byte append at 173 new tokens against a measured 12,936 (deficit_ratio 0.659), so the cost was invisible to admission control as well as to the agent.
- Session recordings and session jsonl files are available for measurement: ~/.llm-proxy/session-recordings/ and ~/.pi/agent/sessions/.

## Candidate approaches, cheapest first

1. Measure first: rank tool results by bytes/tokens across recorded sessions to identify which tools dominate (skill-body pastes, wl show --json dumps, file reads). Deterministic script, no model call.
2. Truncate with re-read: a Pi extension intercepts a tool result above a threshold, keeps head and tail plus an explicit "truncated N bytes, re-read with offset/limit" marker, and preserves the raw output on disk.
3. Reference instead of inline: content-address large or repeated payloads (skill bodies, already-read files) and substitute a short handle plus preview when the content is already in the prompt.
4. Small-model compaction at the boundary: the extension detects an oversized tool result and asks a small/fast model to compact only what the current request needs, prefixing the tool output with a purpose-built instruction. Must reuse the existing summariser slot (Qwen2.5-7B preset, parallel=1, as pinned by the proxy compaction_summarizer) so it does not contend with the main model, and must only escalate here when approaches 2 and 3 are insufficient, since it is a model call on the critical path.
5. Structured projections at the tool level: JSON field selection, summary-by-default with details on demand, and flags that keep payloads small at source.

## Constraints

- Compaction must be cheaper than the prefill it avoids. Measured saving: avoiding 13k prefill tokens saves roughly 45-90 s at observed rates, so a ~2 s small-model call is a clear win; the strategy must be justified against that budget.
- It must not lose information the agent later needs, and any lossy step must be recoverable (raw payload retained and re-readable).
- It runs on the same GPU as the workload it protects, so it competes for capacity -- another reason to prefer non-model approaches first.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: A measurement report exists ranking tool-result payload size by tool and session, produced by a committed deterministic script (no model calls), with the top offenders named.
- AC2: Each of the five candidate approaches is assessed for (a) bytes/tokens saved, (b) added latency and GPU contention, (c) information-loss risk and recoverability, with a recorded recommendation.
- AC3: At least one non-model mechanism (truncate-with-re-read or reference-instead-of-inline) is prototyped as a Pi extension and validated against a real oversized tool result, with the before/after prompt-token counts recorded.
- AC4: If a small-model compaction path is implemented, it reuses the existing summariser slot, is benchmarked against the prefill cost it avoids, and includes a documented fallback when the summariser is unavailable.
- AC5: Documentation states the extension's threshold, behaviour and how an agent recovers truncated content, and the result is recorded against the originating LLM-repo prefill-pricing item.
data.title: Reduce large tool-call results before they enter conversation history

# Intake brief — implement finish changed-scope gate always falls back to the full suite

**Priority:** high · **Issue type:** chore (process/tooling; no gameplay behaviour change) ·
**Status:** CONFIRMED — producer answered Q1 (a), Q2 "as recommended" (= d), Q3 (a) on 2026-11-01.

**Decision (producer, 2026-11-01):** *verify-and-narrow*. The filed premise no
longer reproduces against the installed skills; this item now proves the scoped
gate works in a real `implement.py finish`, documents the node/vitest selection
order, and records the wall-clock measurement. Residual selector gaps are
**out of scope here** and filed on framework item **SA-0MVL7YOMJ006UMDO**
(comment `SA-C0MVXW2CB8003BXPJ`); no agent-infrastructure edits from this repo.

## Problem statement

`implement.py finish` is documented to validate **changed scope only** for fast
iteration, but at filing time every finish gate in this repository logged
`changed-scope selection unavailable … falling back to full scope` and then ran
the full Vitest suite (≈ 346–409 s loaded, plus host-wide test-slot queueing).

Read-only verification during intake shows the **skill-level fix landed after
this item was filed** and the fallback no longer reproduces: the installed

of the last 25 commits. What has *not* happened is proof in a real gate (no

This item delivers exactly that proof.

  change to run only the affected tests, so the build → test → commit loop
  completes in minutes rather than queueing 1–2 h for a full-suite slot.

  deliberately broken affected test, and the full suite to remain the

## Goal (user story)

*As an agent finishing a work item*, I need a slot waiter to take **any** free
slot in its namespace no matter how long it has been waiting, so a green change
is never blocked for hours while capacity sits idle (SA-0MVWKZ4QD006L2E0).

## Context

`Semaphore._try_acquire_slot()` (`skill/shared/process_semaphore.py`) probes
only `range(self.max_workers)`, and `max_workers` is resolved once in
`__init__`. A waiter that started when the pool held two slots therefore never
sees slots `2..7` created later by higher-ceiling processes — the observed
105-minute stall. The poll cadence is already bounded (50 ms base, jittered
`[0.5, 1.5]x`); there is **no** unbounded backoff in the shipped code. The
defect is the fixed-index probe.

This is the implementation slice; it turns the strict-`xfail` regressions from
the two test children green by removing their markers.

## Scope

`skill/shared/process_semaphore.py`:

1. **Dynamic discovery.** Replace the `range(self.max_workers)` probe with a
   namespace scan: each attempt enumerates the numeric slot files currently
   present in the slot directory (deterministic ascending index order) and
   `flock`s the first free one. Slots created by a later, higher-ceiling
   process are therefore usable.
2. **Effective-ceiling rule.** The effective pool is the **union of slot files
   present** in the namespace; the caller's own `max_workers` is a *floor it
   guarantees* (it still creates `0..max_workers-1`), never a host-wide limit it
   may exceed. `_ensure_slots()` stays bounded by `max_workers`.
3. **Fail-fast stays fail-fast.** `timeout=0` performs one scan plus one
   `flock` attempt — no sleep, no blocking work added by the scan
   (`audit_runner` enters with `timeout=0`).
4. **Bounded cadence documented.** Keep the existing 50 ms base and jittered
   `[0.5, 1.5]x` retry; document the maximum poll interval (75 ms jittered, 50 ms
   unjittered) and that no backoff may grow without a documented cap. Record the
   measured directory-scan cost (a single `scandir()` of a directory with ~10
   entries) in the docstring or a comment.
5. **Docstring contract.** The module docstring documents the discovery rule,
   the effective-ceiling rule and the maximum poll interval.
6. **Preserve** the kernel-`flock` model (no PID bookkeeping, no stale locks, no
   daemon), jitter (`SA-0MVEDOF7A004TSWD`) and nested-run isolation
   (`SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86`).

## Constraints

- **Do not change the configured ceiling.** `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` /
  `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_FAST` semantics stay as shipped (`SA-0MVTET8KQ0031R6Z`).
- **Do not implement ordering/fairness.** The FIFO turnstile is owned by
  `SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI`; the discovery scan must remain compatible with a future
  ticket layer (do not restructure acquisition into a queue).
- **Do not touch the `slot_busy` notice** — it keeps meaning genuine saturation.
- **Remove the strict `xfail` markers** added by the two test children as part of
  this slice.
- UK English; no ad-hoc suite invocations (`/skill:test`).

## Repo note

The affected code is this repository's framework source, consumed by other
projects via `scripts/install_pi.sh` and the `~/.pi/agent/skills` symlink. Run
`implement.py start SA-0MVWKZ4QD006L2E0` **from this checkout** so the worktree is
a SorraAgents worktree and `wl` resolves the `SA-*` item against this store.


## Key Files

- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — discovery scan, effective-ceiling and poll-interval docstring contract.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_process_semaphore.py` — strict `xfail` markers removed; regressions green.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_concurrency_guard.py` — cross-process regression green.
- `skill/test/tests/test_test_skill_semaphore.py` — saturation notice regression must stay green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** A waiter whose ceiling is 2 acquires a free slot with index `>= 2` that already exists in the namespace, within one poll interval plus one `flock` attempt.
- **AC2** A waiter still creates at most its own `max_workers` slot files (`0..max_workers-1`); it never creates higher-index slots.
- **AC3** `timeout=0` remains fail-fast: exactly one scan plus one attempt, no sleep, no added blocking work (asserted by test).
- **AC4** The strict `xfail` markers from both test children are removed and all their assertions pass.
- **AC5** Jitter (`SA-0MVEDOF7A004TSWD`) and nested-run isolation (`SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86`) behaviour is unchanged — their existing tests still pass.
- **AC6** The module docstring documents the discovery rule, the effective-ceiling rule and the maximum poll interval (including the measured directory-scan cost); no backoff without a documented cap.
- **AC7** `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` / `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_FAST` semantics and the `slot_busy` notice are untouched; build plus changed-scope tests pass via `/skill:test`.
- **AC8** The full project test suite passes for the change (enforced by the dev-push gate; any gate-reported failure is triaged per the test-failure policy, not worked around).

> The block below restates the parent criteria this child satisfies (parent item
> SA-0MVWKZ4QD006L2E0). It is the machine-checkable coverage mapping, not additional
> child criteria.

### Acceptance Criteria — parent coverage (restated)

- **Parent AC1** — Bounded acquisition once any slot in the namespace is free: a waiter that began polling when only slots 0..N-1 existed must acquire within a documented bound (one poll interval plus one flock attempt) as soon as any slot file in its namespace is free, including slot files created by a later, higher-ceiling process; a max_workers=2 waiter acquires one of the new slots created after it began polling, well inside its timeout.
- **Parent AC2** — Documented maximum poll interval, no unbounded backoff: the poll cadence has a documented maximum interval (50 ms base, jittered 0.5-1.5x when jitter is enabled) and a test pins that a long-waiting consumer still observes slots created after it began waiting (many poll cycles, not one); no backoff may grow without a documented cap.
- **Parent AC3** — Genuine saturation still reports slot_busy: when every slot in the namespace is held for the whole TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT, the test skill still raises TestConcurrencyTimeout carrying the slot_busy notice code and the existing staggered-retry guidance; the no-slot notice must not be weakened or renamed.
- **Parent AC6** — Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Migrated from AH-0MVXVADEL005XNWM (AI_Hell worklog)
This work item was migrated to SorraAgents because all implementation code lives in this repo. Original tracking (comments, evidence, session history) lived on AH-0MVXVADEL005XNWM in the AI_Hell worklog and is preserved in the sections below.

## Problem

The plan skill's autoplan pre-check is meant to decide whether an item needs planning from its effort/risk. On this epic (8 planned children, multi-week scope) the pre-check reported:

- `effort: "Extra Small"`, `risk: "Low"` → `decision: "skip"`.

The zeroed estimate was written by the plan helper's own estimator call, not derived from the item:

```python
# skill/plan/plan_helpers.py :: run_effort_and_risk
payload = json.dumps({
    "issue_id": target_id,
    "o": 0, "m": 0, "p": 0,
    "certainty": 100,
    "assumptions": ["Auto-generated by autoplan decision"],
    "unknowns": [],
})
```

`orchestrate_estimate.py` faithfully aggregates that zero payload, so every autoplan run stamps:

- `effort: XS`, `risk: Low`, PERT `O=M=P=0.00h`, "No detailed WBS items provided".

Evidence: comment `AH-C0MVXV4TGO0066OWH` on AH-0MVWJQUN6009IS87 ("T-shirt size: Extra Small … Recommended (with overheads): 0.00h"), and the follow-on `# Auto-Plan Decision` comment `AH-C0MVXV4TVH003G62N` ("Decision: proceed to implement (effort and risk below threshold)").

## Impact

- `plan_helpers.py plan-if-needed` returns `skip` for **every** item, so the "small item" auto-skip path is indistinguishable from "the estimator wrote zeroes" — planning can be silently skipped for epics.
- The stored `effort`/`risk` fields are overwritten with false values, so the plan-approval gate (`Extra Large` + `High`/`Severe`) can never fire on real risk, and downstream scheduling reads a wrong estimate.
- Observed twice on this item: intake's autoplan pass and the plan session's pre-check both consumed the zeroed estimate.

## Expected behaviour

The autoplan estimate must not overwrite a work item's real effort/risk with a zero payload. Either:

1. derive the estimate from the item + its children (aggregate child WBS rows, count ACs/files), or
2. when no WBS/estimate inputs exist, leave `effort`/`risk` **unset** and return `decision: "error"`-equivalent "unknown" so the plan skill defaults to full planning (its documented conservative fallback), rather than writing `XS`/`Low`.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `plan_helpers.run_effort_and_risk` no longer posts `O=M=P=0` / `XS` / `Low` for an item that has children with non-trivial scope; a regression test covers an epic with children.
2. When the estimator has no real inputs, the work item's existing `effort`/`risk` are left unchanged and `plan-if-needed` falls back to full planning (or a documented `decision: "unknown"`), instead of `skip`.
3. A unit test asserts the pre-check returns `plan` for an epic whose children exist even if the estimator produces no numbers.
4. Existing plan_helpers tests still pass (full suite via the test skill).

## Key files

- `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` — `run_effort_and_risk`, `make_autoplan_decision`, `plan_if_needed`
- `skill/effort-and-risk/scripts/orchestrate_estimate.py` — aggregation / zero-payload handling
- `skill/plan/tests/` — autoplan decision tests

## Related

- discovered-from:AH-0MVWJQUN6009IS87 (observed while planning the optimisation pass — AI_Hell worklog).
- Related (different root cause, already fixed): SA-0MSIUJQAK008AQV8 — only guards the *worklog-lookup-failure* path; the general zeroed-payload path remains.

## Plan (plan skill session, 2026-11-01)

**Implementation repo.** Every path in *Key files* above is relative to the
SorraAgents repo (`/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents`); `skill/plan/` does not
exist in the AI_Hell checkout. The `AH-` item remains resolvable from SorraAgents
tooling through the shared prefix-to-sibling worklog scan
(`skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py::_find_worklog_dir_by_prefix`), so the fix can
be implemented in a SorraAgents worktree while tracking remains on this AI_Hell
work item.

**Reproduction observed during this session (2026-11-01T17:15Z).** Running the
pre-check against this very item reproduced the defect on itself:

- before the run the item's `effort` and `risk` fields were empty;
- `plan_helpers.py plan-if-needed AH-0MVXVADEL005XNWM` returned
  `{"decision": "skip", "effort": "Extra Small", "risk": "Low"}`;
- the same run posted the zeroed `# Effort and Risk Report`
  (`O=0.00h, M=0.00h, P=0.00h`, "No detailed WBS items provided") and the
  `# Auto-Plan Decision` comment, and overwrote `effort`/`risk` with
  `Extra Small` / `Low`.

Those two bogus comments and fields are superseded by the genuine estimate posted
at the end of this planning session.

**Implementation sketch (test-first, one vertical slice).**

1. *Tests first* — `skill/plan/tests/test_plan_helpers.py`:
   - epic-with-children case: an item with children and non-trivial scope must not
     yield `XS`/`Low`; `make_autoplan_decision` must not post the zeroed
     effort/risk report or the autoplan decision comment, and `plan-if-needed`
     must return `plan`.
   - no-real-inputs case: the item's existing `effort`/`risk` are left unchanged,
     no zero payload is written, and the decision is `plan` (never `skip`).
2. *Helper* — `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py`:
   - `run_effort_and_risk`: replace the hard-coded `o=m=p=0` / `certainty=100`
     payload with inputs derived from the item (children's stored effort/risk,
     child and AC counts), and return `None` instead of calling the orchestrator
     when no real inputs exist.
   - `make_autoplan_decision`: treat a `None` result as unknown → `do_plan=True`,
     write no `effort`/`risk`, and post no zeroed report/decision comment.
   - preserve `is_effort_risk_computed` idempotence: the unknown path must not
     write an `autoplan-decision-hash` comment, so a later run can still compute a
     genuine estimate.
3. *Defence in depth* — `skill/effort-and-risk/scripts/orchestrate_estimate.py`:
   only if needed, refuse or annotate an all-zero `o=m=p` payload rather than
   aggregating it into a confident `XS`/`Low`.
4. *Docs* — record the unknown-fallback in the plan skill pre-check section and in
   `docs/dev/plan-skill-reference.md` (SorraAgents).
5. *Verification* — run the `skill/plan/tests` scope through the test skill, then
   manually re-run `plan-if-needed` against an item with empty `effort`/`risk` and
   confirm it returns `plan` and leaves the fields unchanged.

**Vertical slice.** No phasing is needed: the test, helper and doc changes ship as
a single end-to-end slice. No child work items were created.

**Note on AC 2 (clarification, not a rewrite).** The existing plan-skill decision
vocabulary is `skip` / `plan` / `error`; introducing a fourth `unknown` value
would break callers such as the autoplan dispatcher. AC 2 is therefore read as: the
*behaviour* is "unknown → full planning", expressed as `decision: "plan"`,
optionally with an explanatory `reason`/log line — the zero-write behaviour is the
observable "unknown" signal.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No producer questions were asked in this session: the description's ACs and the
*Expected behaviour* section already resolve the issues that would otherwise have
needed an interview. The following are recorded as open questions/assumptions so the
implement session (and the Producer) can confirm them.

- **OPEN QUESTION (implementation repository) — directed to the Producer.** All
  *Key files* live in the SorraAgents repo, but this item is tracked in the AI_Hell
  worklog. *Assumption applied:* implement in a SorraAgents worktree and keep the
  work item here (prefix-to-sibling wl resolution makes `wl` work from either
  checkout). *Why it matters:* `implement.py start` selects the worktree from the
  repo it is invoked in, and `implement.py finish` refuses changes made outside that
  worktree — so the implement session must start in SorraAgents, not AI_Hell.
  *Alternative:* move/mirror this item into the SorraAgents worklog.
- **OPEN QUESTION (derive vs. unknown) — directed to the Producer.** AC 1 asks for
  no zero payload "for an item that has children with non-trivial scope"; AC 2
  allows an unset/unknown fallback. *Assumption applied:* derive from children's
  stored `effort`/`risk` when they exist, otherwise leave the fields unset and fall
  back to full planning. *Why it matters:* the derive path needs a defined
  aggregation rule (sum of child recommendations vs. max t-shirt vs. PERT).
  *Evidence:* `skill/effort-and-risk/scripts/orchestrate_estimate.py` aggregates
  `items`/`o`/`m`/`p`; child items currently carry no WBS rows, so in practice
  most runs will take the unknown path until estimates are propagated.

Discovered while running `/skill:ship release` on 2026-11-02: the audit runner cannot
produce a persistable verdict for a subset of `in_review` items, so the release audit
gate can never pass for them. Two distinct defects compound.

discovered-from:AH-0MVZ6GSMY000VJMH (release-blocking recovery run)

## Defect 1 — Phase 2 / verdict re-ask fail with provider connection errors

Re-auditing these items fails identically on every attempt (4 attempts each on
2026-11-02, including serial runs with `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY=1`):

- AH-0MVXWEDOH002LO1M
- AH-0MVXWEE3L004SPTC
- AH-0MVXWEEJM00813GK

```
Pi provider error: Connection error.
AUDIT_RELIABILITY_SUMMARY calls=3 parse_ok=0 parse_failed=0 timeouts=0
  child_skips=0 provider_errors=3 concurrency_waits=0 verdict_reasks=1 elapsed_seconds≈140
```

Phase 1 completes ("No code quality issues found"); **Phase 2 (deep analysis) and the
verdict re-ask both fail** and nothing is parsed. Observed error contexts in
`~/.audit_debug/AI_Hell/audit_debug_<id>.jsonl`: `{"context":"phase2_deep",
"reason":"provider_error"}` and `{"context":"verdict_reask","reason":"provider_error"}`.

**Not a provider outage:** in the same window a direct `pi -p "Reply with exactly: OK"`
returns `OK` immediately, and 20 other audits in the same pre-flight run succeeded. The
failing items' debug JSONL files are ~2 MB versus far smaller for the successes —
strongly suggesting an oversized request or an unbounded prompt/context is being sent
and the proxy drops the connection.

**Secondary observation:** the reported `AUDIT_RELIABILITY_SUMMARY` (`elapsed_seconds`,
counts) is byte-identical across separate runs, which suggests the "Phase 2 skipped —
small, low-risk item" / script-failure path is replaying a cached summary rather than
reporting the current attempt. Worth verifying: a plausible reading is that a stale
abort-recovery state file short-circuits each retry.

## Defect 2 — verdict persistence rejects the assembled content

For the same items, `wl audit-show` stores a notice instead of a report:

> The audit pipeline completed, but the final persistence step rejected the assembled
> verdict content (malformed JSON / validation error). The full report could not be
> stored in the audit text field.

So even when Phase 1 produced a usable report, the verdict is unreadable by the gate,
and the item is permanently classified as needing a re-audit. The message says "A
re-audit may be required if the verdict data is needed in this field", but re-auditing
deterministically reproduces it (Defect 1).

## Impact

The audit gate (`check-audit-gate.js` / `check-final-validation.js`) treats these as
missing/stale audits, so remediation is attempted, fails, and the release blocks with
exit 6 and later exit 12 — with no path to green short of the runner being fixed. This
made the 2026-11-02 release impossible to complete.

## Environment

- `PI_PROVIDER=Local Proxy` (ContextHub `src/start.ts` proxy, 3-slot pool)
- audit runner: `~/.pi/agent/skills/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
- concurrency during the run: another project (`SorraAgents`) was running
  `audit_runner.py issue --audit-children` concurrently, so saturation may contribute —
  but the failure reproduced serially with `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY=1` and with no other
  AI_Hell audit running.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — For each of the three affected items, `audit_runner.py issue <id>` completes
  Phase 2 and records a parseable verdict (`parse_ok > 0`, `provider_errors == 0`);
  the raw provider-connection-error path is either fixed (e.g. bound the request size /
  chunk or truncate the payload) or fails with an actionable message naming the cause.
- AC2 — A completed audit's verdict is persisted and readable via `wl audit-show` for
  the affected items (no "persistence notice" instead of a report); a test covers the
  malformed-content rejection path.
- AC3 — `AUDIT_RELIABILITY_SUMMARY` reflects the current attempt rather than replaying a
  previous run's numbers, and a stale abort-recovery state file cannot silently short-
  circuit a retry (test-covered).
- AC4 — Re-auditing the three affected AI_Hell items after the fix yields a genuine
  verdict, and the 2026-11-02 release audit gate clears them.

## Files / references

- `~/.pi/agent/skills/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (Phase 2 / verdict re-ask / persistence)
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py` (persistence validation)
- `~/.audit_debug/AI_Hell/audit_debug_AH-0MVXWEDOH002LO1M.jsonl` (repro advice artefacts)
- Ship-skill gate: `~/.pi/agent/skills/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js`

## Plan (2026-11-03) — decomposition

Effort/risk pre-check: `decision=plan` (effort Small, risk High); the plan-approval gate
returned `request_approval=false`, so no approval pause was required. Six children were created
in test-first dependency order. Evidence for the direction is in the "Plan investigation"
comment on this item.

| # | Child | Type | Depends on |
|---|-------|------|------------|
| C1 | Test: failure-notice report must persist with the verdict header first (AH-0MW0K9KAS005L2FM) | task | — |
| C2 | Fix: persist failure-notice reports header-first with truthful diagnostics (AH-0MW0K9KZ6003IEQ3) | bug | C1 |
| C3 | Test: per-attempt reliability summary and stale-state retry safety (AH-0MW0K9LN5006RVBH) | task | — |
| C4 | Fix: bounded slot-aware provider-error recovery for Phase 1/2 and verdict re-ask (AH-0MW0K9M84004UZJ2) | bug | C3 |
| C5 | Docs: audit persistence header rule and provider-error diagnostics (AH-0MW0K9MS8003TG23) | docs | C2, C4 |
| C6 | Verify: re-audit the three affected AI_Hell items and clear the gate (AH-0MW0K9NGN009JSYY) | task | C2, C4 |

AC coverage: AC1 → C4 (+C6 live proof), AC2 → C1 + C2, AC3 → C3 + C4, AC4 → C6.

### Assumptions (confirmed by producer, 2026-11-03 — Q1/Q2/Q3 answered A)

- **Implementation repo.** The audit skill lives in the framework repository
  (`skill/audit/...`; `~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to `SorraAgents/skill`); this AI_Hell
  checkout has no `skill/` tree. The children therefore expect implementation in that
  repository on `dev`, with commits referencing this work item id — the same pattern as
  `AH-0MUFGUYFC001A2OB`. If the producer prefers a mirrored `SA-` work item, the children can be
  migrated before implementation starts.
- **AC1 direction.** The "oversized request / truncate the payload" example is not supported by
  the evidence (5.7–6.7 KB prompts with a succeeding 6.3 KB sibling, and the captured prompt

- **AC4 substitution.** The 2026-11-02 gate cannot be replayed (release `9feeaf42` merged and the

## Goal

Make a failure-notice audit persist its real report instead of the persistence notice, and
make any residual persistence failure tell the truth about why.

**User story:** As the release producer, when an audit call fails transiently I want the
verdict that *was* produced to be stored and readable via `wl audit-show`, so the audit gate
sees a verdict rather than an unreadable notice.

## Context / evidence

See the parent work item's plan investigation. Root cause: `FailureNotice.wrap()` puts the
banner on line 1, while `wl update --audit-text` requires `Ready to close: Yes|No` first
(`audit-invalid-first-line`). `persist_audit` then stores
`_build_fallback_text(...)` with a "malformed JSON / validation error" explanation that is
factually wrong. `wl audit-set` already stored the full report in `rawOutput`, so only the
audit-text field is degraded.

## Scope

- In `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py`: submit the report to `wl update --audit-text`
  with a valid verdict header as the first non-empty line (e.g. keep/relocate the
  `Ready to close:` line to the top, or move the failure banner immediately below it) so a
  `FailureNotice`-wrapped report is accepted. Prefer fixing at the assembly/persist boundary
  and keep the banner fully visible in the body.
- Replace the generic notice wording with the real failure: capture the wl stderr/error code
  (`audit-invalid-first-line`, other validation errors, E2BIG/file-flag fallback) and state
  the cause plus the concrete remediation. Keep `PERSIST_CONTENT_INVALID` semantics for the
  genuine malformed-content case only.
- Keep the salvage pass and the large-report `--audit-file` path working; do not change
  verdict semantics, do not invent verdicts.
- Do not regress the identity/readback guards or the no-stage-bump rule.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — A failure-notice-wrapped report (banner + full per-AC report) is persisted into the
  audit text field; `wl audit-show` shows the report, not the notice.
- AC2 — `rawOutput` preservation and the "Ready to close" verdict are unchanged by the fix.
- AC3 — When persistence genuinely fails, the stored notice names the actual error cause and
  the remediation (no false "malformed JSON" claim); a test asserts this.
- AC4 — Existing persistence tests (`test_persist_audit_resilience.py`,
  `test_persist_audit_large_report.py`, `test_persist_audit_identity.py`,
  `test_persist_audit_no_stage_bump.py`) stay green.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py`
- `skill/scripts/failure_notice.py`
- `skill/audit/tests/test_persist_audit_resilience.py`
- `skill/audit/tests/test_persist_audit_large_report.py`

## Notes

- Implementation repo: framework repo `skill/audit`; commit references this work item id.
- Blocked by the regression-test child (test-first).
- **Producer decision (2026-11-03, Q2 = A, Q3 = A):** the persistence fix is approved as
  specified; implement in the framework repo `skill/audit`, commit on `dev` referencing
  AH-0MVZCXOVE000QKGD.
- **Parent AC2 (persistence clause) — traceability restatement** (covered by this item): a completed audit's verdict is persisted and readable via `wl audit-show` for the affected items (no "persistence notice" instead of a report)

> **Migrated 2026-11-03 from the AI_Hell worklog item `AH-0MW0K9M84004UZJ2`.** The fix lands in this
> repository (`skill/audit` — `~/.pi/agent/skills` symlinks to this repo's `skill/`
> tree), so the work is tracked here under `SA-0MW0LR0D70034DGE`. The original AI_Hell item
> (`AH-0MW0K9M84004UZJ2`) remains a superseded mirror on a producer hold.

## Goal

Make Phase 1, Phase 2 deep analysis and the verdict re-ask survive transient Local Proxy
connection failures (bounded, slot-aware retry) and, when they truly cannot, fail with an
actionable message that names the cause instead of a generic "Connection error." verdict.

**User story:** As the release producer, I want a large-context audit to either complete or
tell me exactly why it could not (phase, attempt count, elapsed, provider/pool cause), so a
transient proxy hiccup cannot permanently block a release with no diagnosis.

## Context / evidence (from the parent plan investigation)

- The failing prompts measured 5.7–6.7 KB — smaller than a succeeding 6.3 KB sibling — and the
  exact captured prompt replays with HTTP 200 today. The "oversized request / truncate the
  payload" hypothesis is **not** supported.
- Retries failed in 11–387 ms (`stopReason: error`, "Connection error."), i.e. fast connection
  failures inside Pi's 2 s/4 s/8 s auto-retry budget, while the Local Proxy (3-slot pool) was
  serving another project's audit. `_PHASE2_MAX_RETRIES = 1` and the Phase-1 budget give no
  slot-aware backoff, and the verdict re-ask has no retry of its own.
- The provider-error path marks every AC `partial` with "Pi provider error: Connection error."
  and sets `ctx.script_failure`, which then triggers the Defect 2 persistence path.

## Scope

- Add a bounded, slot-aware recovery policy for provider *connection* errors in
  `phase2_deep`, `phase2_child`, `phase2_batch`, the Phase-1 parent/child screens and
  `verdict_reask`: a small number of retries with increasing backoff that yield the concurrency
  slot (so parallel audits do not retry-storm a saturated pool), capped so a single item cannot
  hang a release.
- Distinguish "proxy/pool unavailable" from a content/parse failure, and surface it in the
  report evidence with the phase, attempt count, elapsed seconds and the underlying error text.
- Give the emitted `AUDIT_RELIABILITY_SUMMARY` a per-attempt identity (run id and/or started-at
  timestamp, appended to the stable key set) so an operator can always tell whether the numbers
  they are reading came from the attempt they just ran — and so a stale stored report cannot be
  mistaken for the current attempt.
- On exhaustion, the failure must be actionable: name the phase, the model/provider and the
  observed error, and state the remediation (re-run when the proxy pool has capacity,
  `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY=1`, `--force`). Never mark an execution-dependent AC `met` on this path.
- Keep the size-cap safety net optional: add a configurable request-size guard only with a
  documented limit and a measured justification (do not truncate criteria silently).
- Do not change verdict semantics or the canonical report format.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — A provider connection error during Phase 2 (and during the verdict re-ask) is retried
  with bounded slot-aware backoff; a recovered attempt yields `parse_ok > 0` for the ACs in
  tests that simulate a transient connection failure followed by success.
- AC2 — When retries are exhausted the failure evidence names the cause (provider + phase +
  attempts + elapsed) and the remediation; it is not a bare "Connection error." line.
- AC3 — Phase 1 and Phase 2 budgets stay bounded (no unbounded retry loop), the existing
  reliability counters (`provider_errors`, `verdict_reasks`, `timeouts`) still reflect the
  attempt accurately, and the summary line carries a per-attempt identity so a previous run's
  numbers/report cannot be mistaken for the current attempt.
- AC4 — The three target items, re-audited with `--force`, complete Phase 2 with
  `parse_ok > 0` and `provider_errors == 0` (see the verification child).

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_provider_error_reporting.py`
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_json_contract_reask.py`
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_phase2.py`
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_phase1.py`

## Notes

- Implementation repo: framework repo `skill/audit`; commit references this work item id.
- Blocked by the reliability/stale-state test child (test-first).
- If a real request-size limit is ever measured, raise a follow-up item rather than guessing a
  truncation bound here.
- Parent AC1 is satisfied by this child (bounded recovery + actionable failure), not by
  payload truncation.
- **Producer decision (2026-11-03, Q1 = A):** the recovery + actionable-diagnosis direction is
  approved; do not add request truncation. **Q3 = A:** implement in the framework repo
  `skill/audit`, commit on `dev` referencing AH-0MVZCXOVE000QKGD.
- **Parent AC1 — traceability restatement** (covered by this item): for each affected item `audit_runner.py issue <id>` completes Phase 2 and records a parseable verdict (`parse_ok > 0`, `provider_errors == 0`); the raw provider-connection-error path is fixed and, if it still fails, fails with an actionable message naming the cause
- **Parent AC3 (diagnostic clause) — traceability restatement** (covered by this item): `AUDIT_RELIABILITY_SUMMARY` reflects the current attempt rather than replaying a previous run's numbers

## Goal

Prove the fix end-to-end on the three items that were permanently un-auditable on 2026-11-02,
and record the gate classification so the parent's AC4 is verifiably satisfied.

**User story:** As the release producer, I want the three previously un-auditable AI_Hell items
to carry a genuine, readable verdict and to be classified as passing by the audit gate, so I
know the release cannot be blocked by this defect again.

## Context

- Affected items (AI_Hell worklog): `AH-0MVXWEDOH002LO1M`, `AH-0MVXWEE3L004SPTC`,
  `AH-0MVXWEEJM00813GK` — currently `completed`/`done`, `readyToClose: false`, audit `summary`
  = the persistence notice, `rawOutput` = the last (provider-error) report.

# Vitest failures are reported as `unparsed` infrastructure, never as structured test failures

## Problem

`run_tests.py` parses structured failures for every non-pytest command with
`parse_node_failures()` (`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`), which only
understands **Node TAP** output (`not ok <name>` lines). Vitest's default
reporter emits `FAIL |browser (chromium)| <path> > <test name>` plus a
`⎯⎯ Failed Tests N ⎯⎯` block, so a genuine vitest failure yields
`failures: []`.

Consequences observed live on `tce-main-street` (MS-0MVTEVLL000948T1,
2026-11-03):

- `implement.py finish` reported `reason: unparsed`, `notices:
  ["suite exited 1 with no parsable failures: all"]`, `failures: []`,
  `exit_code: 1` for a run whose stderr plainly contained
  `⎯⎯ Failed Tests 1 ⎯⎯ / FAIL |browser (chromium)| … / Error: Timed out
  waiting …`.
- The message therefore told the operator "infrastructure condition, not a
  code failure … the command or its configuration is the problem, not a
  test", which is wrong: two real browser test failures had occurred.
- The classifier's documented contract ("Structured failures always win: a
  genuine failure is never reported as infrastructure") is not met for
  vitest projects, which are the majority of the Node-side suites in this
  estate.
- The gate's facts (`configured_timeout`, `elapsed_seconds`,
  `slot_wait_seconds`, `exit_code`) were correct, so only the failure
  extraction is missing.

## Evidence

```
$ python3 ~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py finish MS-0MVTEVLL000948T1 --json
test_phase: {"reason": "unparsed", "failures": [],
             "notices": ["suite exited 1 with no parsable failures: all"],
             "configured_timeout": 3600, "elapsed_seconds": 427.8,
             "slot_wait_seconds": 0.0, "exit_code": 1}
command: npm --silent test && npx vitest run --project browser tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts && …
```

stderr (same run) contained:

```
⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯ Failed Tests 1 ⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯
 FAIL  |browser (chromium)| tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts > MainStreetScene browser tests > allows pressing Enter to end the turn when legal
Error: Timed out waiting for Turn Summary dialog after end-of-turn presentation after 40000ms (cap 16000ms)
 ❯ waitForCondition core/tests/helpers/waitForCondition.ts:165:8
 ❯ tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts:657:4
```

## Desired change

- Add a vitest failure parser (default reporter `FAIL … > <test>` headers with
  the following `⎯⎯ Failed Tests` blocks, and the `junit`/`json` reporter as a
  fallback) selected when the resolved command runs vitest — the same way
  `parse_pytest_failures` is selected for pytest.
- Keep the fallback order: structured failure → classified infrastructure
  reason; a parsable vitest failure must never be reported as `unparsed`.
- Regression test: a fixture stderr containing a vitest `Failed Tests` block
  yields one structured failure, and the gate classifies it `test_failure`
  with a non-empty `failures` list.
- Also cover `npx vitest run --project browser <file>` command shapes, since
  the project label appears inside the FAIL header.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A vitest failure block produces a structured failure record (test name, excerpt, stack trace), unit-tested against a captured fixture.
- [ ] `implement.py finish` classifies such a run as `test_failure` (not `unparsed`) with a non-empty `failures` list, proven by a gate-classification test.
- [ ] A genuinely unparsable non-zero run still falls back to `unparsed`/`killed` as today (no regression to the infrastructure vocabulary).
- [ ] Documentation (`docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`, `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`) states which reporters are parsed.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVTET8KQ0031R6Z` — timeout/kill/unparsed classification and the deciding
  facts; this item closes the "genuine failure reported as infrastructure" gap
  in that contract.
- `MS-0MVTEVLL000948T1` (tce-main-street) — validation run that surfaced it;
  red findings were triaged as `MS-0MW0M7TR0008GB1O` and `MS-0MW0M7UHT005CY6U`.
data.title: Vitest failures are parsed as unparsed infrastructure, not structured test failures
